subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Bullwhip Effect
description: A 60-second lesson on The Bullwhip Effect.

hook.text: A 5% increase in store sales caused a 40% spike in factory orders. The signal got amplified at each stage.

buildup.text: The bullwhip effect is the amplification of demand variability as orders move upstream in the supply chain.

discovery.text: Each node overreacts—adding safety stock, batching orders—turning a small change into a massive swing.

twist.text: The bullwhip isn't caused by demand itself. It's caused by how companies react to demand signals.

climax.text: Sharing real-time POS data across the chain reduces the bullwhip by giving every tier the same signal.

punchline.text: Stop amplifying the signal. Share it instead.

quiz.question: What causes the bullwhip effect?
options: Order amplification at each supply chain stage
